title: Your First Rock Beat
description: Kick, snare and hi-hat: the three sounds behind the beat you've heard in a thousand songs.

steps.title: Three sounds, one beat
steps.description: Put on almost any rock or pop song and you'll hear the same simple pattern. Count "1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and". The hi-hat ticks on every count, the kick thumps on 1 and 3, and the snare cracks on 2 and 4. That's it. We'll get each sound under your fingers first, then put them together.

steps.title: Hit the kick
steps.description: Find the kick and give it a hit. That low thump is the heartbeat of the groove.
steps.hint: Look for the red pad labelled KCK, top left.

steps.title: Now the snare
steps.description: Hit the snare. Hear how it cuts through? That crack is what makes you want to nod your head.
steps.hint: It's the orange pad labelled SNR, right next to the kick.

steps.title: And the hi-hat
steps.description: Hit the closed hi-hat. It's the quiet tick that keeps time between the bigger sounds.
steps.hint: The green pad labelled CHH, third along the top row.

steps.title: Kick with the hat
steps.description: Hit the kick and closed hi-hat together. That's how beat 1 sounds, and beat 3 too.
steps.hint: They don't have to be perfectly at the same moment. Get them close and it counts.

steps.title: Snare with the hat
steps.description: Now hit the snare and closed hi-hat together. That's beats 2 and 4, the backbeat. Go back and forth between this and the last step and you're playing a rock beat.
steps.hint: Use two fingers, one on each pad, and press down together.

steps.title: Where does the snare go?
steps.description: You're counting "1, 2, 3, 4" through a basic rock beat. Which counts get the snare?
